description: Développeuse web et mobile (Flutter), avec des compétences en ML et DL, je participe en solo. Projet AstroVitals : une app mobile hors ligne qui suit la santé des astronautes et utilise une IA embarquée pour détecter les anomalies et proposer des actions.
summary: Astro Assistant is an offline onboard health assistant for deep-space crews. On the way to Mars, a message to Earth takes up to 22 minutes, so no flight surgeon can react in time. Our platform monitors each astronaut's vital signs, radiation dose, sleep, stress and exercise, and an onboard AI engine detects anomalies, explains why, and proposes a step-by-step protocol, while the crew medical officer always makes the final decision. The engine combines 13 clinical rules with one Isolation Forest model per astronaut, trained on that person's own baseline. In our simulator evaluation it detected 19 of 19 injected anomalies with zero false alerts over 306 crew-hours, in 36 ms per analysis with a 1.2 MB model. Thresholds are grounded in real data: NASA Curiosity RAD radiation, NASA DONKI solar events, NOAA GOES proton flux, and PhysioNet and WESAD physiology. A ground dashboard receives summaries with the real communication delay, and everything keeps working with no network.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Astro Assistant is an onboard health monitoring platform for long-duration missions, built for crews that cannot rely on Earth in real time.

- Crew app: personal health status in under 3 seconds, vital signs, daily check-in, radiation dosimetry, vigilance test (PVT), step-by-step protocols and an emergency mode.

- Crew medical officer (CMO) view: whole-crew dashboard, live alert queue with explanations, medical records, pharmacy, archives and a tamper-evident audit trail (SHA-256 chain).

- Ground link: store-and-forward packets and ground instructions with the real one-way delay (12 to 22 min for Mars). The ground sees events after the crew has already acted.

- Fully offline: the onboard system keeps working with no network.

HOW THE AI WORKS (no external AI API, everything runs on board)

Every reading goes through a 5-step pipeline: cleaning, a 14-day personal baseline (the last 3 days are excluded so an ongoing drift does not become "normal"), features, detection, then explained scores.

Detection combines:

- 13 clinical rules whose thresholds come from real data and literature;

- one Isolation Forest per astronaut (unsupervised anomaly detection), trained on that person's own data. No labelled data of sick astronauts exists, so a supervised model is not possible.

Warnings must hold over two consecutive readings, which filters out isolated spikes. Every alert shows the rule, its top 3 factors and a recommended protocol, and only the CMO can acknowledge or close it.

RESULTS

- Simulator evaluation: 19/19 injected anomalies detected, 0 false alerts over 306 crew-hours, 36 ms median inference, 1.2 MB model per astronaut.

- Real data: our stress rule was tested on WESAD (15 people). Under stress, heart-rate variability falls to 63% of baseline. The 80% threshold catches 62.5% of stress windows, and the rule also requires self-reported stress or short nights to avoid false alerts.

- SpO2 and heart-rate thresholds were checked on PhysioNet BIDMC (53 patients), and the sleep threshold on Sleep-EDF (102 nights).

- Limits: the simulator results are optimistic, real flight data would score lower. This is a prototype, not a certified medical device.

TOOLS

Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, SQLite, scikit-learn (Isolation Forest), pytest (97 tests) · Nuxt 4, Vue, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js · Planned next step: a Flutter mobile app with on-device AI (TensorFlow Lite) connected to wearables.

Sensors are simulated for the demo, because real emergencies cannot be triggered on demand. Real sensor readings enter through the same API endpoint.

REPOSITORIES

Backend and AI engine: https://github.com/alexis-fokam/astroassistant-backend

Frontend: https://github.com/alexis-fokam/astroassistant-frontend
